answer: Ask what a clone farm cannot buy in bulk, and the answer points at Merkle inclusion of the draft in a public log. It requires a draft proven to sit inside a public log, so the haven of scaling up is a queue of real-world chores. Scale stops helping the attacker here. Ten clones need ten separate proofs, each with its own a draft proven to sit inside a public log, and the ledge grows linearly while the reward per clone stays flat. Each clone pays the full price again — no bulk discount, no shared proof — and the ocean is exactly why the farm stays small or goes broke.
